title: Azure App Service Plan CPU and Memory

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `mscs:azure:metrics` events with `resourceType="Microsoft.Web/serverfarms" (metric_name="CpuPercentage" OR metric_name="MemoryPercentage")` into `index=azure`. Confirm UC-4.2.28 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `mscs:azure:metrics` traffic without `resourceType="Microsoft.Web/serverfarms" (metric_name="CpuPercentage" OR metric_name="MemoryPercentage")`. Confirm UC-4.2.28 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

references.title: Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Cloud Services

knownFalsePositives: Short spikes at deploy time, autoscale thrash, or a noisy neighbor on shared hosts can look bad for a few minutes. We require the condition to last across several intervals or clear on its own before we wake someone.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=azure`.
• Install and configure Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Cloud Services with the modular input for `mscs:azure:metrics`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.2.58.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Configure Azure Monitor diagnostic settings or metrics API to export App Service Plan metrics (CpuPercentage, MemoryPercentage) to Event Hub or storage. Ingest via Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices. Alert when CPU or memory exceeds 80% for 5+ minutes. Scale up plan or optimize app code. Distinguish plan-level metrics from app-level (requests, response time).
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:metrics" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:metrics" resourceType="Microsoft.Web/serverfarms" (metric_name="CpuPercentage" OR metric_name="MemoryPercentage")
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.28_azure_app_service_plan_c_28"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `mscs:azure:metrics` in `index=azure` to detect azure app service plan cpu and memory. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_2_28_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Line chart (CPU and memory % by plan over time), Table (plan, metric, avg %), Gauge (current utilization)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Cloud Services and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
